reasoning_traces.think:
The Lp spaces are constructed from measurable functions satisfying integrability conditions. For p ≥ 1, Lp consists of functions whose |f|^p is integrable. The quasi-metric ρp(f,g) = (∫|f−g|^p dμ)^(1/p) fails to satisfy strict positivity because ρp(f,g)=0 does not imply f=g pointwise, only f=g μ-a.e. This motivates identifying functions that differ only on sets of measure zero. The space L1 is complete under this identification, forming a Banach space. Hölder’s inequality generalizes Cauchy-Schwarz and provides bounds for products of functions in Lp and Lq where 1/p + 1/q = 1. It ensures that fg ∈ L1 whenever f ∈ Lp and g ∈ Lq, which is essential for defining inner products and norms in functional analysis. These structures enable rigorous treatment of limits, continuity, and convergence in infinite-dimensional spaces relevant to signal processing and statistical inference.
